name: instance-derive-grants
title: tests(instance): derive write grant from create-only filesystem policy
body:
### What
Pins `derive_contract_grants`: a create-only filesystem policy derives the `filesystem.**` write grant while read stays ungranted.

### Why it matters
Create implies mutation; dropping the create arm or requiring both lists silently unmediates creation paths. Existing recipes always set read+write+create together, so the create-only edge is unpinned.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| drop `|| !filesystem_create...is_empty()` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| `||` -> `&&` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-instance --lib create_only_filesystem_grants`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.

name: instance-validate-identifier
title: tests(instance): pin id and hostname identifier validation edges
body:
### What
Pins `validate` identifier rules for both id and hostname: empty/spaced rejected, dotted alnum accepted, hostname checked independently.

### Why it matters
Hostname defaults to id, so suites that never set a distinct hostname cannot detect a skipped hostname check. Removing either validation call survives today.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| skip `validate_identifier(self.id...)` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| skip `validate_identifier(self.hostname...)` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-instance --lib validate_pins_identifier`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.

name: instance-override-id
title: tests(instance): pin instance.id override and unknown-key rejection
body:
### What
Pins the `instance.id` override arm: quoted values apply, hostname re-derives, unknown keys and unquoted values fail closed without partial mutation.

### Why it matters
Deleting the arm or making it a no-op silently ignores operator overrides; existing tests pin vcpus/hostname but not id.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| delete `instance.id` arm | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| arm parses but discards value | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-instance --lib override_instance_id`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.

name: instance-override-resources
title: tests(instance): pin memory override application and exact bounds
body:
### What
Pins the `resources.memory_mib` override: value applies, exact lower bound 16 accepted, 15 rejected atomically, quoted numbers rejected.

### Why it matters
Override arms are fail-closed config gates; deleting the memory arm or its validation admits invalid configs. Existing override tests pin vcpus but never memory.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| delete `resources.memory_mib` arm | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| `16..=` -> `15..=` in validate | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-instance --lib memory_override_enforces`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.

name: process-pipe-ends-guards
title: tests(process): pin pipe_ends zero for invalid and dead pipes

mutants.name: no-live

body:
### What
Pins `pipe_ends`: pipe 0 and out-of-range ids report 0, live pipes report their end count, freed slots report 0, reused slots report fresh counts.

### Why it matters
Diagnostics drive leak checks; dropping the zero guard indexes pipe 0 - 1 (underflow) and counting dead slots misreports leaks. No existing test exercises these edges.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| disable `pipe == 0` guard | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| drop `.live` check in pipe_ends | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-process --lib pipe_ends_reports`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.

name: process-retain-refcount
title: tests(process): pin duplicate retain counts and source-close survival

mutants.name: retain-nolive

body:
### What
Pins `retain` via duplicate: both duplicated ends raise the count to 4, closing originals keeps the pipe alive, only the last copy frees it.

### Why it matters
Over-retaining leaks pipe objects; skipping the live check retains freed slots. Existing duplicate tests pin single-end retention, not both-ends survival.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| `ends += 1` -> `ends += 2` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| drop `.live` check in retain | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-process --lib duplicate_retains`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.
